versions.short: The bill would require the Federal Aviation Administration to publish and keep up to date a public list of medications that pilots, air traffic controllers, and people training for those jobs may safely take or be prescribed for medical certification, and that the FAA has approved for those purposes. The list would be developed after consulting pilot and controller groups, flight schools, aviation medical experts, and other stakeholders, and would show allowed medications, their contraindications, whether FAA review is needed, and medications designated as Do Not Issue or Do Not Fly. It would also be made available through the MedXPress system, indicate how long someone may need to limit duties while stabilizing on a medication if practicable, and include a way for doctors to contact the FAA with questions. The FAA would update the list when relevant guidance changes, and publishing the list would not make the agency liable for harm from someone relying on it.
